描述_ZN: Song Mountain Three Queues", early Qing dynasty topography, combined with "Tai Muro Shique Inscription", "Shao Muro Shique Inscription" and "Kaimu Temple Shique Inscription". It is a white paper framed book, with thick ink topography, 7 and a half pages in total, decorated with brocade surface. Taimuro Que inscriptions" 2 openings, 14 lines per opening, 9 characters; "Shaomuro Que inscriptions" 3 and a half openings, 10 lines per opening, 6 characters; "Kaimu Temple Que inscriptions" 2 openings, 10 lines per opening, 4 characters. With Zhu Yi container inscription, collection of 2 seals.　　"Song Mountain Three Que" is the combined name of Tai Muro Stone Que, Shao Muro Stone Que and Kaimu Temple Stone Que, which are located in Song Mountain area of Henan Province and are the most ancient temple queues existing in China.　　Taimuro Stone Que is located in the Zhongyue Temple in Mt. The inscription was engraved in the fifth year of the first year of Emperor An of the Eastern Han Dynasty (118). The main text is written in 27 lines, with 9 characters in the third line and 10 characters in the third line. The front of the tablet is in seal script. Shaomuro Stone Que is located at the eastern foot of Shaomuro Mountain, west of Dengfeng County, Henan Province, and is a Shinto que in front of Shaomuro Shao Aunt Temple, carved in the second year of Emperor An's Yanguang (123) in the Eastern Han Dynasty. Its south side is engraved with an inscription in seal script, with 22 lines and 4 characters. The front of the tablet is in seal script. The stone queue of Kaimu Temple is also known as the stone queue of Qimu Temple, which was changed from "QI" to "KAI" to avoid the taboo of Emperor Jing of Han Dynasty Liu Qi. It is located in the north of Dengfeng County, Henan Province, under the Ban Ban Feng Peak, and is the temple of the gods of Qimu Temple, engraved in the second year of the Eastern Han Dynasty Emperor Yan Guang (123). Seal script 32 lines, no forehead. The inscriptions of "Song Mountain Three Queues" express the worship of the mountain gods.　　The font of "Tai Muro Shiqu" is wide and circumscribed, simple and elegant, with strong and majestic clerical style; the seal script of "Shaomuro Shiqu" is broad and simple, with a wang yang style; the calligraphy style of "Kaimu Temple Shiqu" is similar to that of "Shaomuro Shiqu", but the font is slightly smaller and the style is square and ancient. Shaomuro Stone Queue Inscription" and "Kaimu Temple Stone Queue Inscription" are among the top quality Han seal carving stones. Kang Youwei once said, "There are only two kinds of Han seal tablets left, such as "Shaomuro" and "Kaimu", which can be considered as the world's greatest treasure and the top instrument of seal script."　　The book of "Jinshifu", "Jinshifu Zuizhi Zuizhi", "Good Book of Stele and Poster", "Ma Ziyun, Shi Anchang, "Identification of Stele and Poster", etc. were recorded by Gu Yanwu in Qing Dynasty.
